name: DOLK-CDG (dolichol kinase, CDG-Im)
aliases: congenital disorder of glycosylation type Im

reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A dolichol-pathway CDG caused by deficiency of dolichol kinase, which phosphorylates dolichol to dolichol phosphate, the essential lipid carrier for glycosylation
Classically presents with dilated cardiomyopathy, sometimes in relative isolation, which can dominate the clinical picture and lead to heart failure
A severe multisystem form with ichthyosis, seizures, hypotonia and early death is also recognised, reflecting phenotypic heterogeneity
Because dolichol phosphate is needed to assemble the lipid-linked oligosaccharide, the biochemical defect produces a type I transferrin pattern
Cardiac involvement can present without the prominent neurological picture typical of many other CDGs, so CDG should be considered in unexplained infantile cardiomyopathy
Management is supportive, including heart failure care and consideration of transplantation for end-stage cardiomyopathy, coordinated with metabolic specialists
Diagnosis is confirmed by DOLK molecular genetic testing
reference.pathophysiology: DOLK encodes dolichol kinase, the endoplasmic reticulum enzyme that phosphorylates dolichol to dolichol phosphate. Dolichol phosphate is the obligate lipid anchor on which the oligosaccharide precursor is assembled and is also required for O-mannosylation and GPI-anchor synthesis. Deficiency limits precursor assembly and transfer, giving under-occupied N-glycosylation sites and a type I transferrin pattern. Impaired glycosylation and O-mannosylation of cardiac and other structural proteins is thought to underlie the characteristic dilated cardiomyopathy and, in severe forms, the cutaneous and neurological features.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of infantile dilated cardiomyopathy (mitochondrial, storage, genetic sarcomeric)
Other dolichol-pathway and type I CDG subtypes (e.g. DPM1-CDG, SRD5A3-CDG)
Congenital ichthyosis syndromes when skin involvement predominates
Barth syndrome and other metabolic cardiomyopathies
Carnitine and fatty acid oxidation disorders
additionalInvestigations: Transferrin isoelectric focusing or mass spectrometry showing a type I pattern
Echocardiography and cardiac assessment for dilated cardiomyopathy
Neuroimaging and electroencephalography when neurological features are present
Skin assessment for ichthyosis in severe presentations
redFlags: Signs of heart failure or a new dilated cardiomyopathy in an infant
Severe ichthyosis with a multisystem, rapidly deteriorating course
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is largely determined by the cardiomyopathy, which can progress to end-stage heart failure and early death; the severe multisystem form carries high infant mortality, whereas more isolated cardiac disease may be amenable to heart failure treatment or transplantation.
pitfalls: Not considering CDG in apparently isolated infantile dilated cardiomyopathy
Assuming a normal neurological examination excludes a glycosylation disorder
Overlooking the coagulopathy before cardiac procedures
Expecting a specific pharmacological cure when care is supportive
references: Scriver's OMMBID, dolichol pathway disorders of glycosylation
Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics, disorders of glycosylation
management: No specific disease-modifying therapy; management is supportive and coordinated with metabolic specialists
Heart failure therapy for the dilated cardiomyopathy with diuretics, angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers and beta-blockers as tolerated
Consideration of cardiac transplantation for end-stage cardiomyopathy
Antiseizure medication and neurological supportive care in the severe multisystem form with seizures and hypotonia
Emollients and skin care for ichthyosis, with nutritional support
Monitor with serial echocardiography, coagulation studies and liver function given multisystem involvement
Multidisciplinary team including cardiology, metabolic medicine and paediatrics
Genetic counselling and family testing given autosomal recessive DOLK inheritance
